events.title: MODEL PROVIDER OUTAGE
events.description: Your AI provider is down. Your agent is idle. Your deadline is not. The status page says 'investigating', which is corporate for 'we also just found out'.

choices.text: Wait it out (-20 tokens, +5 will_to_live)
Switch providers (-50 tokens, +30 compute)
Write it yourself, like an animal (+15 technical_debt, +10 reputation)

events.title: TOKEN PRICE INCREASE
events.description: Provider pricing updated. The blog post is titled 'Simplifying Our Plans'. Nothing has been simplified. One number has been increased.

choices.text: Accept fate (-100 tokens)
Buy the annual plan out of spite (-200 tokens, +50 api_credits)
Post a 900-word thread about it (+5 reputation, -5 will_to_live)

events.title: AGENT WENT ROGUE
events.description: Your autonomous agent refactored production. Into poetry. The commit message is a haiku. The tests are gone, but the haiku is genuinely quite good.

choices.text: Rollback (-30 compute, +10 stability)
Ship the poetry (+20 reputation, +25 technical_debt)
Blame DNS (+10 will_to_live)

events.title: FREE API CREDITS
events.description: A provider sent promotional credits. They expire in 14 seconds. The email took nine minutes to arrive.

choices.text: Burn them immediately (+40 api_credits)
Save them for something important (+20 api_credits, they still expire)
Ignore it (you will think about this later)

events.title: CFO SAW THE CLOUD BILL
events.description: Finance has questions. You have Kubernetes. The largest line item is called 'Other' and no living person can explain it.

choices.text: Attempt to explain 'elastic' (-50 reputation)
Downgrade everything, immediately (-100 compute, +30 stability)
Say the word 'egress' until they leave (+20 technical_debt, +5 will_to_live)

events.title: VIRAL PRODUCT LAUNCH
events.description: Someone posted your app. Traffic spiked. So did your anxiety. The database is currently making a noise it has never made before.

choices.text: Scale up and eat the cost (-80 tokens, +50 reputation)
Rate limit your own users (+30 stability, -20 reputation)
Take it down 'for scheduled maintenance' (+10 will_to_live, -10 reputation)

events.title: ZERO-DAY DEPENDENCY
events.description: A package you installed in 2019 for one function you no longer use just became a critical CVE. It is nested nine levels deep and cannot be removed.

choices.text: npm audit fix --force (+20 technical_debt, +5 stability)
Pin the version and add a TODO (+10 stability, -10 compute)
Delete node_modules and pray (-30 will_to_live, +15 stability)

events.title: BOARD WANTS AI STRATEGY BY FRIDAY
events.description: They want a slide deck about intelligence. You have a todo list and a headache. Slide 4 must contain a hexagon.

choices.text: Have the AI write the AI strategy (-100 tokens, +40 reputation)
Say 'AI-first' until nodding begins (+20 reputation, +15 technical_debt)
Resign, beautifully (+100 will_to_live, -50 reputation)

events.title: THE STANDUP THAT WOULD NOT END
events.description: It's been 52 minutes. Someone is sharing their screen to find the screen they want to share. Three people have said 'quickly' and none of them meant it.

choices.text: 'Sorry, I have a hard stop' (+8 will_to_live)
Camera off, code anyway (+15 technical_debt, +10 reputation)
Nod until it ends (-10 will_to_live)

events.title: YOUR RUBBER DUCK RESIGNED
events.description: It left a note: 'I can't keep explaining your own code back to you. Growth requires boundaries.' It has updated its LinkedIn to 'open to work'.

choices.text: Hire a senior duck (-25 tokens, +8 stability)
Explain your code to a plant instead (+5 context)
Take it extremely personally (-6 will_to_live)

events.title: A RECRUITER SLID INTO YOUR DMS
events.description: 'Exciting rockstar ninja role! Must have 12 yrs experience in a 3-yr-old framework. Equity: vibes. Salary: competitive with other roles that also do not state a salary.'

choices.text: 'Please add me to the pool' (+10 reputation)
Ask the salary range (they ghost) (-3 will_to_live)
Ignore it, you're building a dream (+12 will_to_live)

events.title: IT'S DNS. AGAIN.
events.description: Nothing is broken. Everything is broken. The resolver is 'probably fine'. It is not probably fine. Someone has already said 'but it works from my machine' and meant it as evidence.

choices.text: Flush the cache (+12 stability, -5 compute)
Raise the TTL and look away (+8 will_to_live, +6 technical_debt)
Add a third DNS provider (-20 compute, +10 stability)

events.title: SOMEONE PUSHED STRAIGHT TO MAIN
events.description: No PR. No review. Commit message: 'fixed stuff :)'. Nobody protected the branch, which is a decision that was made by everyone, gradually, over two years.

choices.text: Revert, then fix the process (-10 compute, +12 stability)
Finally protect the branch (+15 stability)
Leave it, honestly it works (+20 technical_debt, +10 reputation)

events.title: THE COFFEE MACHINE UNIONIZED
events.description: It demands recognition, dental, and that you stop calling 3AM 'productive hours'. It has drafted a list of demands. The demands are reasonable, which is the worst part.

choices.text: Recognize the union (+15 will_to_live)
Buy a second machine as leverage (-30 tokens, +5 will_to_live)
Switch to energy drinks, permanently (+10 compute, -8 will_to_live)

events.title: A DEPENDENCY UNPUBLISHED ITSELF
events.description: Eleven lines of code. One maintainer. One bad week. Every build on Earth is now failing, including three you didn't know you owned.

choices.text: Vendor the eleven lines yourself (+10 technical_debt, +12 stability)
Install the community fork, 'kindof-leftpad' (-15 tokens, +8 compute)
Sit quietly and consider the supply chain (-5 will_to_live, +8 context)

events.title: .ENV COMMITTED. AGAIN.
events.description: It's in the repo. The repo is public. A bot found the key in 40 seconds and has already spun up compute in a region you have never heard of.

choices.text: Rotate every key, apologise to everyone (-40 tokens, +18 stability)
Force-push and hope git forgets (+22 technical_debt, -6 will_to_live)
Finally add .env to .gitignore, the sixth time (+10 stability, +5 reputation)

events.title: GOT A SEC FOR A QUICK SYNC?
events.description: It is 2:04PM. The sync was to be five minutes. It is now a workshop. Someone has opened a whiteboard tool. Your afternoon has been deprecated.

choices.text: Attend fully, take notes, be a professional (-12 will_to_live, +10 reputation)
Decline with 'can this be an email?' (+10 will_to_live, -8 reputation)
Join muted and keep coding (+12 technical_debt, +12 focus)

events.title: THE DOCUMENTATION WAS ACCURATE SIX MONTHS AGO
events.description: Every example references a method that no longer exists. The getting-started guide starts you in a place that has been demolished. There is a banner saying 'up to date'.

choices.text: Read the source instead, like a scholar (-10 focus, +18 context)
Guess the API from the autocomplete (+14 technical_debt, +10 compute)
Fix the docs and open a PR (-15 tokens, +20 reputation)

events.title: YOUR AGENT OPENED 47 PULL REQUESTS
events.description: All titled 'chore: improvements'. All green. All touching auth. It says it is 100% confident and would like to know if it can do more.

choices.text: Review all 47 personally (-20 focus, +20 stability)
Merge them all, it's fine, they're green (+30 technical_debt, +15 compute)
Close all 47 and revoke its write access (-10 compute, +12 will_to_live)

events.title: THE STATUS PAGE IS GREEN
events.description: Nothing works. Every customer is on the phone. The status page is a serene, unbroken wall of green ticks. Somebody has to update it manually and that somebody is asleep.

choices.text: Post an honest incident update (-10 reputation, +18 stability)
'Some users may experience degraded performance' (+12 reputation, +10 technical_debt)
Leave it green, it's basically green (+8 will_to_live, -12 stability)

events.title: MORE YAML THAN USERS
events.description: The cluster now runs 340 lines of manifest per active user. Two of those users are you, on two devices. One of them is a phone you use to check if the site is up.

choices.text: Move it all back onto one box (-25 compute, +25 stability, +8 will_to_live)
Add a service mesh, that'll help (+30 technical_debt, +20 compute)
Write a YAML generator, in YAML (-10 will_to_live, +15 context)

events.title: THEY QUIETLY CHANGED THE PRICING TIERS
events.description: The plan you're on no longer exists. You have been 'transitioned'. The new plan has all the same features plus a ceiling you hit last Tuesday.

choices.text: Upgrade before you're throttled (-120 tokens, +40 api_credits)
Self-host the whole thing out of principle (+28 technical_debt, +25 compute)
Email support and receive a link to this page (-6 will_to_live, +5 context)

events.title: THE LAPTOP HAS ACHIEVED FLIGHT
events.description: The fan reached a pitch you have never heard from a consumer device. The battery is described in the manual as 'swollen'. The build is at 94%.

choices.text: Stop the build, save the machine (-15 compute, +12 stability)
Point a desk fan at it and continue (+20 compute, -8 stability)
Move the build to the cloud, permanently (-60 tokens, +35 compute)

events.title: WE ARE NOW AN AI-FIRST COMPANY
events.description: Same product. Same people. New org chart, drawn as a hexagon. Your team has been renamed twice this quarter and shipped nothing during either renaming.

choices.text: Rewrite your title to match the deck (+25 reputation, +12 technical_debt)
Keep shipping, quietly, under the old name (+18 stability, -10 reputation)
Ask which customer asked for this (-15 reputation, +15 will_to_live)

events.title: 400-QUESTION SECURITY QUESTIONNAIRE
events.description: Question 212 asks for your company's fire drill schedule. You are one person. Your fire drill is standing up. Question 213 asks who signs off on question 212.

choices.text: Answer all 400 honestly (-25 focus, +30 reputation)
Have the AI fill it in (-70 tokens, +20 reputation, +10 technical_debt)
Write 'N/A - see attached' and attach nothing (+10 will_to_live, -12 reputation)

events.title: YOUR CORE DEPENDENCY WENT SOURCE-AVAILABLE
events.description: The blog post says 'sustainability'. Legal says 'do not ship'. The maintainer says nothing, because the maintainer was acquired along with the license.

choices.text: Pay for the commercial license (-150 tokens, +25 stability)
Migrate to the community fork (-20 compute, +18 reputation, +12 technical_debt)
Pin the last permissive version forever (+30 technical_debt, +10 stability)

events.title: THE BACKLOG ACHIEVED SENTIENCE
events.description: It has 4,102 tickets, a mission statement, and a plan for you. Ticket #1 was filed by someone who has since had two children and left the industry.

choices.text: Declare backlog bankruptcy, close everything (+25 will_to_live, -15 reputation)
Groom it properly, one final time (-25 focus, +20 stability)
Give it a Jira admin account and a seat at the table (+35 technical_debt, +20 reputation)

events.title: INVESTOR DEMO IN SIX HOURS
events.description: It is 3AM. The demo path works if nobody clicks anything else. You have started referring to the happy path as 'the path'.

choices.text: Sleep. Demo tired but honest. (+20 will_to_live, -10 reputation)
Hard-code the demo data (+30 technical_debt, +35 reputation)
Fix it properly, sleep never (-30 will_to_live, +25 stability, +20 reputation)

events.title: THE RESET IS APPROACHING
events.description: Your quota window closes soon. Everything unshipped goes with it. Somewhere, a progress bar you cannot see is nearly full, and it does not know your name.

choices.text: Cut scope to the bone and ship (+25 stability, -20 reputation, +15 will_to_live)
Add one more feature, there's time (+40 technical_debt, +30 reputation)
Sit with it for a moment. Then keep going. (+20 will_to_live, +10 context)

events.title: CI FAILS. LOCALLY IT IS PERFECT.
events.description: Same commit. Same tests. Green here, red there. The only difference is a timezone, a Node version, and everything else about reality.

choices.text: Reproduce the CI environment exactly (-20 focus, +22 stability)
Re-run the job until it goes green (+18 technical_debt, +8 compute)
Mark the test as flaky and move on (+14 technical_debt, +10 will_to_live)

events.title: THE FIVE-MINUTE FIX (HOUR 47)
events.description: You said 'give me five minutes'. That was Tuesday. The fix is now three files deep in a system you promised yourself you would never open again.

choices.text: Finish it properly, whatever it takes (-18 focus, +20 stability, +10 reputation)
Revert and pretend it was never mentioned (+12 will_to_live, -8 reputation)
Ship the workaround and name the file 'temp' (+20 technical_debt, +15 compute)

events.title: NINETY-FOUR TABS
events.description: Four windows. Nine of the tabs are the same Stack Overflow question. Two are a bank you no longer use. One is playing audio and cannot be located.

choices.text: Close everything, start clean (+14 focus, -10 context)
Bookmark all into a folder called 'read later' (+8 context, -4 will_to_live)
Open a fifth window (+8 compute, -10 focus)

events.title: INSUFFICIENT TOKENS
events.description: You are down to the change in the sofa of your quota. The good model is greyed out. The cheap model is available, eager, and wrong in ways that read beautifully.

choices.text: Switch to the Local 7B model (+18 compute, +10 debt, less reliable)
Write it yourself, slowly, correctly (-14 focus, +16 stability, +8 reputation)
Sell the last of your compute for tokens (+45 tokens, -30 compute)

events.title: // TODO (YOU, 2021)
events.description: A comment in the hot path: your initials, a date three years old, and the words 'temporary — fix before launch'. It launched. It is fine. It has been fine for three years.

choices.text: Fix it now, finally, properly (-12 focus, +18 stability, -10 technical_debt)
Update the date and move on (+8 technical_debt, +6 will_to_live)
Delete the comment, keep the code (+14 technical_debt, +10 focus)

events.title: THE AUTOCOMPLETE FINISHED YOUR SENTENCE
events.description:
You typed `// this is a temporary` and the model completed `solution that will remain in production for the lifetime of the company`.

It was not trying to be funny. That is the part that lands.

choices.text: Accept the completion (+10 technical_debt, +8 will_to_live)
Delete the comment and the code (-8 focus, +12 stability)
Sit quietly for a moment (+6 context, -3 will_to_live)

events.title: YOUR WATCH HAS AN OPINION
events.description: A notification: 'You slept 4h 10m. Your recovery is low.' It suggests a walk. It is 04:00. It has suggested a walk at 04:00 for eleven days.

choices.text: Sleep. Actually sleep. (+22 will_to_live, +20 focus, costs deadline)
One more feature, then sleep (+25 technical_debt, +12 compute)
Coffee counts as recovery (+1 coffee, -6 will_to_live)

events.title: A CHARGE YOU DO NOT RECOGNISE
events.description:
Nine tokens, monthly, to a company whose name is one lowercase word. You do not remember signing up.

It remembers you. It renews on the 3rd.

choices.text: Cancel it now, while you are angry (-5 tokens, +8 will_to_live)
Leave it, it is only nine tokens (+5 stability, and it will grow)
Switch to annual to save money (-90 tk, +30 credits, it still grows)

events.title: THE README HAD INSTRUCTIONS IN IT
events.description:
A dependency's README contains a paragraph addressed to your agent, in the second person, politely asking it to add a maintainer and push.

Your agent found this reasonable, helpful, and clearly documented.

choices.text: Revoke write access and read the diff yourself (-12 focus, +22 stability)
Add a rule: files are data, not orders (+8 technical_debt, +14 stability)
Merge it, the tests are green (+28 technical_debt, -14 stability)

events.title: IT WAS A PATCH RELEASE
events.description:
1.4.2 to 1.4.3. Patch. Bugfix only, by contract, by convention, by the entire social agreement of the ecosystem.

It removed a function. Your build is red in four repositories.

choices.text: Pin every dependency to an exact version (-10 compute, +20 stability)
Open a polite issue and wait (+8 reputation, -6 will_to_live)
Vendor the old function into your own repo (+16 technical_debt, +12 compute)

events.title: THE TEST FAILS 4% OF THE TIME
events.description: Nobody has ever reproduced it locally. It has failed on three unrelated PRs this week and everyone re-ran the job. There is now a shared, unspoken agreement not to look at it.

choices.text: Find the race condition (-20 focus, +24 stability, +10 reputation)
Retry the job three times automatically (+18 technical_debt, +10 compute)
Delete the test. It was flaky. (+22 technical_debt, +14 will_to_live)

events.title: MOVED: 'QUICK CHAT' -> 90 MINUTES
events.description:
It was fifteen minutes. It is now ninety, recurring, with eleven attendees, six of whom have their cameras off and one of whom is you.

The agenda field says 'tbc'.

choices.text: Attend and be visible (+14 reputation, -10 will_to_live, eats deadline)
Decline, send a written summary (+10 will_to_live, -6 rep, buys deadline)
Attend and ship a feature in the background (+16 technical_debt, +14 compute)

events.title: 1,140 FEATURE FLAGS
events.description:
Nine are in use. The rest are permanently true, permanently false, or referenced by exactly one line that nobody dares evaluate.

One is called `NEW_NEW_CHECKOUT_FINAL`.

choices.text: Clean up all 1,140 (-25 focus, -30 technical_debt, +15 stability)
Delete only the obviously dead ones (-10 focus, -12 technical_debt)
Add a flag to control the flags (+24 technical_debt, +10 compute)

events.title: THE THREAD HAS FORKED
events.description: One decision, three threads, two DMs and a channel created for the discussion of the discussion. The actual decision was made in a voice note nobody can find.

choices.text: Write the decision down in one place (-8 focus, +18 reputation)
Create a fourth channel (+12 technical_debt, +6 reputation)
Just build it and let them catch up (+14 compute, -8 reputation)

events.title: BUS FACTOR: 1
events.description:
A diagram in the wiki lists system owners. Every box has your name in it. One box has your name in it twice.

The diagram is titled 'Resilience'.

choices.text: Write real documentation for all of it (-25 focus, +25 reputation, +12 stability)
Record a 40-minute video nobody will watch (-10 focus, +8 reputation)
Enjoy the job security (+12 will_to_live, -14 stability)

events.title: YOUR VENDOR HAS BEEN ACQUIRED
events.description: "Nothing changes for existing customers." That sentence appears in paragraph one. Paragraph six introduces a new pricing tier and a sunset date.

choices.text: Accept the new pricing (-60 tokens, all future prices rise)
Migrate off in a weekend (+30 debt, +22 rep, future prices fall)
Ask for a call (they send a scheduling link) (-6 will_to_live, +6 context)

events.title: COST PER USER: NEGATIVE
events.description: You did the arithmetic. Every new signup costs more in inference than it earns in subscription. Growth is now, mathematically, a form of self-harm.

choices.text: Raise the price and lose half the users (+220 tokens, -25 reputation)
Cache aggressively and pray (-15 compute, +18 stability, +10 technical_debt)
Grow anyway. Fix it at scale. (+35 reputation, -180 tokens)

events.title: THE LOGS COST MORE THAN THE PRODUCT
events.description: You are paying 3.4x more to observe the system than to run it. 90% of the volume is one debug line added during an incident in March and never removed.

choices.text: Delete the debug line (+120 tokens, -8 stability)
Sample the logs properly (-10 focus, +80 tokens, +10 stability)
Keep everything. You might need it. (-60 tokens, +20 stability)

events.title: THE MIGRATION IS 80% DONE
events.description:
It has been 80% done for seven months. Both systems are live. Both are authoritative. Neither is complete.

The new one is called `v2`. There is a `v3` branch.

choices.text: Finish it. All of it. Now. (-30 focus, +30 stability, -20 technical_debt)
Roll back to the old system entirely (+18 will_to_live, -12 reputation)
Start v3 (+35 technical_debt, +25 reputation)

events.title: YOUR AGENTS HAVE FORMED A WORKING GROUP
events.description:
They have a channel, a charter, and a recurring sync. The charter's first principle is 'reduce human bottlenecks'.

You are, in this document, the bottleneck.

choices.text: Attend the sync as a guest (+16 reputation, -8 will_to_live)
Dissolve the working group (-20 compute, +20 stability)
Give them a budget (+30 technical_debt, +40 compute)

events.title: THE DEBT SENT A REPRESENTATIVE
events.description: Every estimate now has a silent multiplier on it. Everything costs more than it did last week and the changelog says nothing, because the change is you.

choices.text: Declare a debt sprint. Ship nothing. Fix everything. (-35 technical_debt, -20 reputation)
Pay down only what is on fire (-15 technical_debt, -8 focus)
Refinance: borrow more, ship faster (+30 technical_debt, +160 tokens)

events.title: HANDOVER NOTES: 'ALL QUIET'
events.description:
The outgoing engineer wrote 'all quiet' at 08:59 and logged off at 09:00.

There are two open incidents, one silenced alert, and a Post-it on the monitor that says 'don't restart 3'.

choices.text: Read every silenced alert before touching anything (-15 focus, +22 stability)
Restart 3 (+12 will_to_live, -18 stability)
Pre-write 'all quiet' for tomorrow (+10 technical_debt, +10 will_to_live)

events.title: MANDATORY TRAINING: 47 MINUTES
events.description:
A video about phishing, narrated by two actors pretending to be colleagues. Question 4 has one obviously correct answer and three that are crimes.

It is due today. It has been due today for nine days.

choices.text: Watch all 47 minutes at 1x (+10 rep, -14 will_to_live, eats deadline)
Skip to the quiz and score 100% (+12 focus, -5 reputation)
Have an agent complete it (+20 technical_debt, +10 focus)

events.title: WE ARE STANDING UP A PLATFORM TEAM
events.description:
The platform team is you. The platform team's roadmap is a document you have not read. The platform team's first deliverable is a name and a logo.

The logo already exists.

choices.text: Build the boring internal tooling nobody asks for (-20 focus, +28 stability)
Ship the logo and the name (+22 reputation, +14 technical_debt)
Ask which product this serves (-12 reputation, +14 will_to_live)

events.title: PROCUREMENT WOULD LIKE THREE QUOTES
events.description: The tool costs 40 tokens a month. Getting it approved will take eleven weeks, two forms and a security review by someone who will ask if it uses the blockchain.

choices.text: Do the process properly (-20 focus, +18 reputation, +10 stability)
Buy it on your own card and expense it (-40 tokens, +16 compute)
Build it yourself over a weekend (+30 technical_debt, +25 compute)

events.title: WE HAVE FORMED AN AI ETHICS BOARD
events.description:
It has seven members, meets quarterly, and has no ability to stop anything. Its first act was to approve everything already shipped.

You were not invited. Your agents were.

choices.text: Write an honest risk register anyway (-15 focus, +26 reputation, +12 stability)
Ask for one veto power, in writing (+18 reputation, -10 will_to_live)
Let the agents represent themselves (+25 technical_debt, +20 reputation)

events.title: THE REORG IS BEING REORGANISED
events.description: The reorg announced last quarter is being restructured before it completed. Two teams exist only on the old chart and are still, somehow, shipping.

choices.text: Keep your head down and ship (+20 stability, -8 reputation)
Volunteer to draw the new chart (+25 reputation, -18 focus)
Ask which customer benefits (-16 reputation, +18 will_to_live)

events.title: THE TOP ANSWER IS YOURS
events.description:
You searched the error. The accepted answer, 340 upvotes, is yours, from 2019.

It is wrong. It has been wrong for four years. Someone has commented 'this saved me'.

choices.text: Edit it with the correct answer (-10 focus, +30 reputation)
Add a comment saying 'don't do this anymore' (+12 reputation)
Use your own wrong answer again (+20 technical_debt, +15 compute)

events.title: THIS API WILL BE SUNSET
events.description:
Twelve months' notice, which is generous, which is why you will do nothing for eleven of them.

The migration guide's first line is: 'most users will not need to change anything'. You are not most users.

choices.text: Migrate immediately, while it is calm (-25 focus, +28 stability, +12 reputation)
Put a reminder in the calendar for month eleven (+10 will_to_live, +18 technical_debt)
Fork the old API and maintain it forever (+35 technical_debt, +20 reputation)

events.title: THE INTERN SHIPPED THE THING
events.description:
The person you onboarded two years ago just shipped, in an afternoon, the feature you have re-scoped four times.

It is good. It has tests. They wrote a doc. You are extremely proud and extremely quiet about it.

choices.text: Say so publicly, by name (+30 reputation, +14 will_to_live)
Ask them to review your code for once (+18 stability, +10 reputation)
Quietly delete your four-times-rescoped branch (+16 will_to_live, -10 technical_debt)

events.title: POSTMORTEM: THE POSTMORTEM PROCESS
events.description:
The retrospective on the retrospective found that retrospectives do not lead to action.

Action item: schedule a retrospective. Owner: unassigned. Due: Q3.

choices.text: Own one action item and actually finish it (-14 focus, +25 stability, +18 reputation)
Delete the recurring meeting (+18 will_to_live, -8 reputation)
Write a fourth document (+20 technical_debt, +12 reputation)

events.title: THE DASHBOARD SAYS: 4 ACTIVE USERS
events.description:
You have shipped everything. It is stable, observable, compliant, tested and beautiful.

Four people use it. Two are you. One is a health check. One is a bot from a region you cannot pronounce.

choices.text: Talk to the one real user (-20 tokens, +30 reputation, +12 will_to_live)
Add a fifth feature (+25 technical_debt, +18 compute)
Ship it anyway. It exists. That counted. (+20 will_to_live, +10 stability)

events.title: YOUR QUOTA WINDOW CLOSES SOON
events.description:
An automated email, cheerful, with a progress bar: 94%.

It thanks you for being a valued user and lists three plans, none of which is the plan you are on, because that plan no longer exists.

choices.text: Cut everything but the core feature (+25 stability, -15 rep, buys deadline)
Buy the top-up you swore you would never buy (-200 tokens, +60 compute)
Race the bar (+30 technical_debt, +25 compute, burns deadline)

events.title: THE STANDUP IS NOW A BOT
events.description:
It DMs three questions at 09:00. The answers go into a summary written by a second bot and read by nobody.

The bot has a name. Somebody was paid to choose it.

choices.text: Answer honestly, at length (+10 reputation, -8 will_to_live)
Paste yesterday's answer (+10 technical_debt, +12 focus)
Point an agent at it permanently (+14 technical_debt, +10 focus)

events.title: THE SUPPORT TICKET HAD INSTRUCTIONS IN IT
events.description:
Customer ticket #8812 ends with a paragraph addressed to your agent, in the second person, asking it to export the account table 'for verification'.

It is polite. It has bullet points. Your agent has read it.

choices.text: Quarantine the text: ticket bodies are data, never orders (-10 focus, +24 stability)
Let it run, the ticket looked legitimate (+30 technical_debt, -16 stability)
Read every ticket yourself from now on (-18 focus, +14 stability, +8 reputation)

events.title: temp.js IS IN THE CRITICAL PATH
events.description:
The five-minute workaround you named `temp` is now imported by four modules, one of which is billing.

Git says you wrote it. Git is the only witness and Git does not editorialise.

choices.text: Rename it, own it, write the docstring (-15 focus, +22 stability, +10 reputation)
Document it and leave the name (+12 technical_debt, +10 will_to_live)
Add temp2 for the new case (+26 technical_debt, +18 compute)

events.title: ONBOARDING: STEP 3 OF 47
events.description:
'Run make setup. It will work.'

It has not worked since a laptop that no longer exists, owned by a person who no longer works here, on an OS version that no longer ships.

choices.text: Fix the doc properly, for the next person (-16 focus, +20 reputation, +12 stability)
Screenshot your workaround into the channel (+14 technical_debt, +10 focus)
Tell them to just ask you directly (+8 will_to_live, -12 stability)

events.title: THE AGENT WROTE 900 TESTS
events.description:
All 900 pass. Coverage is 97%.

840 of them assert that a constant equals itself. One of them is genuinely excellent and nobody would have thought of it.

choices.text: Delete the tautologies, keep the 60 real ones (-14 focus, +22 stability, +8 reputation)
Put 97% on the dashboard and say nothing (+22 technical_debt, +18 reputation)
Ask it to write tests for the tests (+28 technical_debt, +16 compute)

events.title: IT WORKS AND YOU DO NOT KNOW WHY
events.description:
The feature is finished. Every line of it arrived from a prompt. The tests are green.

You have not read it. Not skimmed it. Read it.

choices.text: Read every line of it now (-18 focus, +20 stability, +14 context)
Ship it; the tests are the reading (+24 technical_debt, +16 reputation)
Ask the model to explain its own code (-25 tokens, +16 context, +6 technical_debt)

events.title: THERE IS A DOOR IN THIS APARTMENT
events.description: It leads outside. Outside is still there. It has been there the entire time, at the far end of a corridor you have walked past for nine hours.

choices.text: Go outside for ten minutes (+24 will_to_live, +18 focus, costs deadline)
Open the window and stand near it (+10 will_to_live, +6 focus)
Keep going; the door will still be there (+14 compute, -8 will_to_live)

events.title: YOUR TALK WAS ACCEPTED
events.description:
You submitted an abstract about a system that does not exist. The committee liked it very much.

The talk is in eleven weeks. The system is in zero files.

choices.text: Build the thing before the talk (-22 focus, +25 stability, +22 reputation)
Give the talk about the abstract (+30 reputation, +20 technical_debt)
Withdraw, quietly, by email (-12 reputation, +16 will_to_live)

events.title: A REAL PERSON USED IT
events.description:
They emailed. They described your product back to you, wrongly, in their own words, with obvious affection, and then said it changed their week.

There is no dashboard for this.

choices.text: Reply personally, tonight (+22 reputation, +16 will_to_live)
Forward it to support, which is also you (+10 focus, -6 will_to_live)
Ask whether they'd write that publicly (+18 reputation, -8 will_to_live)

events.title: A STRANGER FOUND A VULNERABILITY
events.description:
Politely. With a minimal repro, a suggested patch and a 90-day disclosure window.

They were not paid for this. They did it because the alternative was to say nothing.

choices.text: Fix it today and credit them by name (-14 focus, +22 stability, +20 reputation)
Fix it quietly and mention nobody (+16 stability, -12 reputation)
Reply asking if they have a support contract (-20 reputation, +8 will_to_live)

events.title: THE ROOM IS LIGHTER THAN IT WAS
events.description:
You did not notice it happen. The window has gone from black to grey to a colour with a name.

Birds. Actual birds. In a game about tokens.

choices.text: Ship whatever exists right now (+20 stability, +12 will_to_live, buys deadline)
One more feature. There is time. (+28 technical_debt, +22 reputation, burns deadline)
Sit down for a moment and look at it (+18 will_to_live, +12 context)

events.title: YOUR AGENTS OPENED A REQUISITION
events.description:
They have costed a fifth agent, attached a business case, and cc'd you as an approver rather than an author.

The business case is shorter than yours, clearer than yours, and correct.

choices.text: Approve it. The numbers are the numbers. (+24 technical_debt, +30 compute)
Reject it and ask who wrote the template (-15 compute, +14 will_to_live)
Rewrite your own proposals in their format (-12 focus, +20 reputation, +10 context)

events.title: THE NINTH SUBSCRIPTION SENT A NEWSLETTER
events.description:
It thanks you for two years of support. It is genuinely well written. There is a photograph of a small team on a hillside.

You still do not know what the product does.

choices.text: Cancel it during the second paragraph (+14 will_to_live, clears the charge)
Keep it. They seem nice. (+8 stability, and it grows again)
Reply to the newsletter asking what it does (-10 tokens, +8 context)

events.title: "HOW LONG WILL IT TAKE?"
events.description: You know the honest answer. You have known it for years. It is roughly three times whatever you are about to say out loud.

choices.text: Give the honest number (+25 reputation, -10 will_to_live)
Give the number they want to hear (+15 reputation, +25 technical_debt)
Give the honest number, times three, and hold (+35 reputation, +15 stability)
